methodological_questions: Can adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix be measured reliably from play-by-play and matchup data?
Is the recommended mix derived out-of-sample, without using the outcomes it is later scored against?
Do 54 series units give enough power to detect an adherence-to-winning association?
Do team quality, opponent quality, injuries, and pace confound any adherence-win association?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether the V4 engine's top pt_shift beats the team's modal play type in a playoff series. Full-calibrated headline 69.8% (37/53); DRIVE-modal comparisons 85.7% (12/14); clean comparisons 64.1% (25/39); high-confidence 64.3% (27/42); uncalibrated archival 51.7% (31/60). Recorded as artifact_found, failure type C_artifact, limited by small sample, with LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks. n=53 scoreable, no bootstrap CI computed. Record text is cut; read_family would give the full text.

Ranked playsheet validation across 10 series. Spearman rho=-0.0639, p=0.099717, n=665 (no clear full-rank signal). Kruskal-Wallis H=32.9723, p=2.7e-05. Mann-Whitney BEST 1.257 (n=56) vs AVOID 1.092 (n=160), p=0.004018. Trigger accuracy rho=0.4525, n=121. Limited by leakage, low measurement reliability, and small sample; mechanism recorded as E_unclear. Record text is cut.

Possession Control Index (PCI) incremental R2 over ORtg as a DRtg proxy. Headline dR2=+0.139, but offensive-control components add only +0.005 beyond ORtg. corr(leakage, DRtg)=+0.894. The baseline omitted defense by construction. Recorded as artifact, C_artifact, with LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risks. This concerns a different question; it is cited only as evidence of how leakage and construction flaws produced apparent effects in this project.

Possession-level test of a proxy engine on all regular-season games. Gamma +0.0714 (SE 0.0057, p=0.0000) for the C model; DiD +0.062 [0.051,0.073]. Proxy agreement with the production engine was 13/79 = 16.5%. Recorded as in-sample contamination of regular-season aggregates, with iid standard errors. Coverage: 9,853 RS pairs; 35.7% clear, 33.8% ambiguous, 30.4% no_rec. Verdict inconclusive.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Scoring the engine's top play-type recommendation against the team's modal play type in playoff series.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact_found (C_artifact), with LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks. Headline accuracy fell from 69.8% (calibrated) to 51.7% (uncalibrated archival), so the apparent effect depended on construction choices. n=53 with no bootstrap CI.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking alternative play types by a playsheet counter ranking and testing whether BEST outperformed AVOID in the next half.
failed_approaches.why: Full-rank Spearman was null (rho=-0.0639, p=0.0997). Only the pairwise BEST vs AVOID contrast was significant (p=0.004). Recorded limits were leakage, low measurement reliability, small sample, and drift/nonstationarity. The mechanism is recorded as unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: A matchup-conditioned play-type picker tested on all regular-season games at possession level.
failed_approaches.why: Proxy fidelity to the production engine was 16.5% (below 70%). The regular-season aggregates were in-sample contaminated, and the standard errors assumed iid observations. Verdict inconclusive.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using a leaky composite (PCI) to explain team outcomes beyond a baseline.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact (C_artifact). The headline gain tracked the outcome through leakage (corr +0.894 with DRtg). The baseline omitted defense by construction. Shows that leakage in composites is a documented failure pattern in this project, not evidence about adherence.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project studies of engine-recommended play types (SF-APPS-003, SF-APPS-018, SF37) did not produce a clean, leakage-free, adequately powered result. SF-APPS-003 is recorded as an artifact and SF-APPS-018 and SF37 as inconclusive.
Leakage in recommendation or composite construction has repeatedly produced apparent effects that did not survive scrutiny (SF-APPS-003, SF-APPS-068).
Proxy fidelity to the production recommender has been low (16.5% in SF37), so a 'recommended mix' built from a proxy may not be the mix the project actually uses.
Sample sizes in the earlier studies were small (n=53 to n=665 at different units), and no earlier study reported a power-adequate series-level adherence test.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence to a suppression-conditional mix predicts series winning. No retrieved record tests adherence against series outcomes with a leakage-free design.
The true size of any adherence-win association or its confidence interval.
Whether the 54-series unit count is sufficient, since no record computed a power analysis for this specific question.
Whether the 2025-26 playoff data, partial as of the question date (2026-06-16), can serve as a holdout.
The full text of the truncated records (SF-APPS-003, SF-APPS-018). Their summaries are cut and were not read in full.
own_inferences: With 54 series and a plausible win-probability difference of about 0.15 between high- and low-adherence groups, power at alpha 0.05 is well below 0.8. Roughly 170 or more series would be needed for a simple two-group comparison, so the design is underpowered.
Adherence is a behavioural measure defined by the recommender, so a recommender that is fit on the same series outcomes will leak. A valid test needs the mix fit on earlier seasons only.

Adherence is confounded with team quality and matchup: stronger teams may both follow recommendations more and win more. Without adjustment, a positive association would not identify a recommendation effect.
The question asks about 'winning' at series level, but the unit of recommendation is the possession or game. Aggregation to series adds noise and lowers power further.
uncertainties: Truncated record text for SF-APPS-003 and SF-APPS-018 may contain details (e.g., calibration choices, exact adherence definitions) that change the assessment. Not verified.
The 54-series count is as recorded by the task; the number of usable series after exclusions is unknown.
Whether the 2025-26 playoffs (complete only from 2026-06-21) can be used at all, given the question date of 2026-06-16.
No earlier record defines an adherence metric or a suppression-conditional mix precisely, so the estimand itself is not fixed.
No retrieved record reports effect sizes for adherence and win outcomes in a clean design.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that earlier project tests of the same recommendation family were recorded as artifact or inconclusive. They were affected by leakage, low proxy fidelity, and small samples. This moved the decision from a plain test toward do_not_proceed, because a test of adherence on these 54 series would repeat the same failure modes without a clean out-of-sample design.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series units are far below what is needed to detect a plausible adherence-to-winning difference at adequate power.
The recommended mix has been fit on the same outcomes it is scored against in prior studies. A valid test needs the mix estimated only on data before each scored series.
Adherence depends on a recommender whose proxy fidelity to the production engine was recorded at 16.5%, so the measured adherence may not be the intended construct.
Team quality, opponent quality, injuries, and pace can drive both adherence and winning, so a raw association would not identify an effect of the recommendations.

prior_work.summary: Related questions have been studied: engine-recommended play types against team modal play types (SF-APPS-003, artifact), playsheet counter rankings (SF-APPS-018, inconclusive), a proxy engine on regular-season possessions (SF37, inconclusive), and a leaky composite index (SF-APPS-068, artifact). None tests whether adherence to a suppression-conditional mix predicts series winning with a leakage-free, power-adequate design. The question is therefore partly answered in the sense that the earlier attempts are documented but not resolved.

risks.text: 54 series units give low power for an adherence-to-winning association.
Recommendation construction may use outcomes from the scored series, inflating apparent adherence-win association, as in SF-APPS-003 and SF-APPS-068.
Adherence measurement depends on a recommender with low proxy fidelity (16.5%) and low measurement reliability (SF-APPS-018).
Team strength, opponent strength, and injuries may drive both adherence and winning.
If 'suppression-conditional' labels are derived from points or outcomes, the recommended mix and the outcome share a source.
Earlier work tested many variants (calibrated/uncalibrated, clean/ambiguous subsets, pairwise contrasts), so the analyst degrees of freedom are large.
Play-type efficiency and team strategy change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so a mix estimated in one season may not transfer.
Series-level win probability is near 0.5 for many matchups, so a small adherence effect may be hard to separate from the base rate.

design.estimand: Minimum viable test: the difference in series win probability between high-adherence and low-adherence team-series, where adherence is measured against a mix fit only on prior seasons (no outcome leakage).
design.unit: Team-series (one team in one playoff series), with adherence aggregated from possession-level records.
design.sample: Pooled 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoffs for fitting the mix. Evaluation on a frozen holdout (2025-26 playoffs), used only after complete data are available (from 2026-06-21 at the earliest). The 54 recorded series are insufficient alone.
design.power: A simple two-group comparison needs roughly 170 or more series to detect a 0.15 win-probability difference at alpha 0.05 and 80% power. The current 54 do not reach this. Power must be recomputed on the actual holdout size before any run.
design.controls: Adjust for pre-series team strength (prior-season rating), opponent strength, injury/availability, and pace. Use cluster-robust standard errors by team. The mix must be fit with no access to evaluation-series outcomes.
design.falsification: Pre-register a null: adherence has no association with series win after adjustment. Also a negative control: adherence to a random or shuffled mix should show no association. Failure of the negative control invalidates the design.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary contrast and a fixed set of secondary contrasts, with Holm correction across them. No post hoc subsets (clean, high-confidence) as headline results.
design.decision_rule: Claim support only if the pre-registered primary adjusted association has a 95% CI excluding zero on the holdout, the negative control is null, and proxy fidelity to the production recommender is at least 70%. Otherwise report as inconclusive or artifact.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs for fitting; 2025-26 playoffs as holdout, frozen at a recorded data snapshot after completion (not before 2026-06-21). Partial 2025-26 data as of 2026-06-16 must not be used.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict winning in NBA series?
What sample size and series-level unit count are needed to test adherence-outcome association?
How should the recommended mix be derived without leakage from outcomes?
What confounders (team quality, opponent, injuries, pace) threaten adherence-to-winning inference?
args.query: suppression-conditional recommended play-type mix adherence predicts series winning NBA defensive suppression counter strategy

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
